issues.legal_issue: Land-ceiling provisions and implementing rules that form part of a land-reform scheme are protected from fundamental-rights challenge.
material_facts: A constitutional petition challenged a land-ceiling provision and an implementing rule on fundamental-rights grounds.
The disputed land was admitted to be a holding under the governing legislation.
The court held that the challenged provision and rule were part of a land-reform scheme.
issues.conclusion: The provision and rule were protected from attack under Article 31A and were valid.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A protects provisions that form part of a land-reform scheme from the asserted fundamental-rights challenge. The Court applied this principle to section 6(xvii) of the U.P. Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1960, and rule 4(4) of the Rules made under it; it cited no earlier cases.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_land_ceiling: A person challenged the validity of a land-ceiling measure on fundamental-rights grounds.
predicates.measure_part_of_land_reform_scheme: The challenged measure formed part of a land-reform scheme.

issues.definition: When a fundamental-rights challenge concerns a land-ceiling measure that forms part of a land-reform scheme, the measure is protected from that challenge.

issues.legal_issue: A delegated rule within the authority conferred by a statute protected under Article 31B is not subject to further fundamental-rights scrutiny.
material_facts: A constitutional petition challenged an implementing rule on fundamental-rights grounds.
The parent legislation was included in the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution.
The court held that the rule did not exceed the authority conferred by the relevant statutory provision read with the Act's rule-making provision.
issues.conclusion: The rule was protected under Article 31B and was valid; it did not require further scrutiny under Articles 14, 19 or 31.
issues.legal_principle: A statutory rule that is within the powers conferred by a section of a statute protected by Article 31B need not be further scrutinised under Articles 14, 19 and 31. The Court applied this principle to rule 4(4), made under section 6(xvii) read with section 44 of the U.P. Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1960, which was included in the Ninth Schedule as item 58; it cited no earlier cases.

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge_to_del: A person challenged the validity of a delegated rule on fundamental-rights grounds.
predicates.parent_law_has_constitutional_schedule_p: The parent law was included in a constitutional schedule that protects it from the asserted challenge.
predicates.delegated_rule_within_enabling_authority: The delegated rule stayed within the authority conferred by the parent law.

issues.definition: When a delegated rule is challenged on fundamental-rights grounds, its parent law has constitutional schedule protection, and the rule stays within the authority conferred by that law, the rule is protected from the challenge.
